  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: The watcher now cancels the timed-out child run before the workflow timeout block reads `/jobs` and posts its own second cancel. The `queued_without_runner` diagnostic can under-report, and the duplicate cancel can print a misleading `Could not cancel timed-out child run` warning.
  WHY: Cancelled jobs stop being `status=queued`, and a repeat cancel on an already-cancelled run can be rejected. The PR cannot fix this because the issue forbids editing the workflow file. Severity disagreement: sonnet, openai and glm rated it NIT, minimax rated it MAJOR (mapped to high), and gemini called it an expected side-effect. The highest rating is used.
- scripts/dispatch_and_watch_workflow_run.sh:376-380 | severity=low | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: The cancel failure warning discards the exit status and stderr. A timeout, a 403, a 404 and a 409 all print the same "Could not cancel watched run" line.
  WHY: Operators cannot tell a transport failure, an auth failure and an already-cancelled run apart. The suggested fix is to capture `cancel_rc=$?` and append ` (exit N)` to the warning. Reviewers rated this a NIT or a hardening suggestion with risk score 1.

- Hardening suggestion (risk score 1): scripts/dispatch_and_watch_workflow_run.sh, lines 378-380. Capture the exit code and include ` (exit ${cancel_rc})` in the warning. About 3 lines changed.
